import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('/data/nls_bmi_processed.csv')
df.head()

from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
import numpy as np

# Prepare the data for logistic regression
X = df[['INCOME']].values.reshape(-1, 1)  # Predictor
y = df['SAMESAVE'].values  # Response

# Create a logistic regression model
model = LogisticRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficient
coefficient = model.coef_[0][0]
p_value = model.pvalues[0]

coefficient, p_value

import statsmodels.api as sm

# Prepare the data for logistic regression
X = df[['INCOME']]  # Predictor
X = sm.add_constant(X)  # Adding a constant term for the intercept
y = df['SAMESAVE']  # Response

# Create a logistic regression model
model = sm.Logit(y, X)
result = model.fit()

# Get the coefficient and p-value
coefficient = result.params['INCOME']
p_value = result.pvalues['INCOME']

coefficient, p_value

from scipy.stats import chi2_contingency

# Logistic Regression using sklearn

# Create a logistic regression model
model = LogisticRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficient
coefficient = model.coef_[0][0]

# Chi-squared test for independence
# Create a contingency table
contingency_table = pd.crosstab(df['INCOME'], df['SAMESAVE'])

# Perform chi-squared test
chi2, p_value, dof, expected = chi2_contingency(contingency_table)
